description: The two-phase method finds all Pareto-optimal paths of a two-objective problem. Phase 1 finds the *extreme supported* solutions, the corners of the convex hull of the Pareto set. It does this by *dichotomic search*: for two neighbouring solutions it minimizes the weighted sum whose level line runs through both, and keeps a new solution below that line. Phase 2 searches each triangle between two neighbours for the other, *non-supported* solutions, with BOA*'s pruning limited to that box. The result is the same as BOA*'s.

papers.title: A comparison of solution strategies for biobjective shortest path problems

papers.authors: José Craveirinha, João Clímaco, Rita Girão-Silva, Marta Pascoal
papers.title: Multiobjective Path Problems and Algorithms in Telecommunication Network Design—Overview and Trends
